v1.feedback: The nocturne word genuinely drove design decisions — slowed rotation, cooled the palette from IKB to midnight indigo, added a reflective water plane — so the parent morph reads as intentional rather than cosmetic. The differential-growth spine from 7wq is clearly preserved and the Whistler reference lands with the silver-ghost reflection below. Two issues: the reflection plane's ripple distortion (sin-based vertex displacement) is too uniform and reads as a cheap mirror trick rather than actual water — consider fragmenting it with a second frequency or fading reflection opacity toward the edges so it dissolves naturally. The upper moonlight gradient (smoothstep 2→12) could be tighter; right now the silver wash feels evenly applied across too much of the form, losing the sense of selective illumination that a real nocturne would have — try concentrating it on the topmost 20% of vertices with a sharper falloff.

v2.feedback: The Whistler silver-over-indigo palette and moonlight-crown gradient are genuine nocturne moves, not just a hue shift — good chain lineage. The reflection plane at 0.03 opacity risks being invisible; bump it to 0.05–0.07 so the water-ghost actually registers as a compositional element. Base plane opacity of 0.06 combined with the sharp moonlight falloff at y=0.78 likely starves the lower 75% of the ribbon of any visible detail — widen the moonlight ramp to smoothstep(0.5, 0.95) or raise uOpacity to 0.09 so the indigo body reads as mass rather than void. The slow auto-rotate earns its compute here; keep it.
